articles.title: “IT IS THE GLORY OF GOD TO CONCEAL A THING”

paragraphs.text: P. van den Berg
Proverbs 25: 1–5

I am seeking help, beloved brethren, in relation to what has been read. The word of God has a very current bearing; whichever part of the Scriptures we read it has a very current bearing as the blessed Holy Spirit applies it to us in relation to the current needs of the testimony. As the brethren well know, the book of Proverbs works out in the woman of worth, who can be trusted. That is a great matter, to be trustworthy in relation to that which we have received.

What God in His grace has recovered us to is to be maintained at all cost. We have here the proverbs of Solomon and I would suggest that that would refer to that which is from the beginning. The brethren know the departure as it is traced in Revelation 2 and 3; it is traced to Ephesus where first love was left. The great height of things was set out at Ephesus; as Paul says, “all the counsel of God” (Acts 20: 27) was brought out. The Lord Jesus in the Revelation traces the departure at Ephesus because the departure is from the highest features of the truth, but then the recovery is to the highest features of the truth. So in Philadelphia we have a recovery, which I doubt not was in the Lord’s own mind from the beginning, to that which was departed from at Ephesus.

We have had a setting out of ministry, beloved brethren, that is related to that which is from the beginning; it is related, as John said, to “That which we have heard, which we have seen ... concerning the word of life”, 1 John 1: 1. John presents to us the Son of the Father’s love, and Solomon sets out the affectionate side in sonship. It is a great thing in every matter of responsibility to have in our hearts the great place the assembly has in the mind of God, the great place we have in sonship associated with Christ in the presence of the Father. In the working out of matters here we must proceed from the highest point, in the dignity that, according to God, has been given to the saints. What greater place could be ours than to be associated with the Son of God in the Father’s presence? I believe administration proceeds from that point. We have in Matthew 17 the Lord Jesus shining as the sun and a voice saying, “This is my beloved Son ... hear him”, and from that point the matter of responsibility in the testimony is met. We see in the close of the chapter how the Lord anticipated Peter as to what he might do and brings the matter to a conclusion in divine wisdom, as the Lord will conclude any matter relating to the testimony, for it is not yours and it is not mine; it is the Lord’s, it is the Lord’s testimony.

So wisdom has a great place in the assembly; the assembly is wisdom’s house, indeed we read in Ephesians 3: 10, 11 that the all-various wisdom of God is made known to the principalities and authorities in the heavenlies through the assembly, according to the purpose of the ages. That is, that in the purpose of God the present time was in view, the world to come was in view, and the eternal state was in view—that is finality; but the present time was in view in the purpose of the ages that there should be a witness, amid the scene of confusion, to divine order in the assembly. And God has recovered us to that. The house of God is not a place of disorder; the house of God is a place of order, and wisdom is working things out in relation to the truth that God has given us, that He has recovered us to.

I would suggest, beloved brethren, that in the men of Hezekiah we have represented those who have served in the recovery to bring out the truth as it was from the beginning, and we do well to give heed to it; we do well to pay heed to the distinct ministry which the Lord has given in the course of the recovery. Hezekiah’s time, as we know, was marked by a wonderful revival. We are in a time of wonderful revival; it may be in outward smallness and weakness, but it is very precious in the mind of God. What mercy it is that as we find ourselves here tonight, beloved brethren, we can trace the living current of the truth as it has proceeded in the recovery. Whatever has happened in the course of the recovery, whatever departure there may have been, Mr. Raven said it can be traced to not holding the Head, and we need Christ as the One who is the Source of all wisdom, power, and food.

So we have this reference here to it being God’s glory to conceal a thing; but the glory of kings is to search out a thing. I would suggest that the king would represent the way that things are worked out in administration. As we all know, administration is not universal; it will be universal; the day is coming, the world to come, when there will be a universal administration in the Man of God’s purpose. But the wisdom of God is seen working out in the present time in local assemblies, and it is a great matter to see how God’s glory is bound up with the assembly. The assembly will be the vessel of divine administration in the world to come when all that is now here in mystery will come out in public display. What a glorious administration it will be! There will not be any unresolved problem in the world to come. But the assembly is already in the light of the world to come and she is already in the light of the eternal state, and it works out in the present time.

The great test as to all truth that is ministered is as to what there is in the way of a practical working out in relation to it. For what would truth be if there was no practical working out of it in administration? I am not afraid to use the word administration; administration is local, and God has given us light and truth to be maintained in faithfulness in the way it is worked out amongst us.

The king would represent that side of things, the line of administration, governed by the prophetic word. The king does not determine the truth, you know; the king is governed by the truth. The kings of Israel were to be governed by the prophetic word; what the prophet said was what they were to do. So the prophetic meeting has an important place, and God is confirming the saints in the prophetic ministry that He gives. We have in Revelation 2 and 3 the prophetic word as it bears on local assemblies in the way that the Lord Jesus appears prophetically to them, each in its own responsibility, each governed by one and the same Person and by one and the same truth, for the truth is one, and the Spirit is One, and Christ is the Head of the assembly. So there is glory working out in the assembly at the present time.

We have this statement here—“It is the glory of God to conceal a thing”. You know, beloved brethren, the natural mind is not able to take in the things of God, and it has pleased God to hide things from the natural mind that are evident to the spiritual mind. “The spiritual discerns all things, and he is discerned of no one”, 1 Corinthians 2: 15. The king is not discerned by anyone. Paul in writing to the Corinthians had to combat the natural mind, and there is nothing more serious and dangerous than the natural mind interfering in the things of God.

The king would know that—it is the glory of kings to search out a thing. How wonderful that God has secured an answer to His eternal thoughts in the assembly, the assembly the vessel of His praise, and there is nothing that tests us like responsibility, because we are here in responsibility, and privilege precedes responsibility. That is one thing we need to have established in our minds, that privilege precedes responsibility. The more we are in the gain of our privilege spiritually the more we shall understand the working out of things in responsibility; that is the glory of kings, the glory of kings is to search out a matter.

The natural mind will not understand. Peter had to learn that he could not rely on his mental capacity in the working out of the truth. The Lord had to rebuke Peter in Matthew 16 when he had just had that wonderful revelation, “Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God”. The Lord said, “Flesh and blood has not revealed it to thee, but my Father who is in the heavens … thou art Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly”. But Peter immediately fails by resorting to the natural mind. Beloved brethren, we cannot be governed by natural feelings in the things of God; we must be governed by the truth, we must be governed by that which God has given as light and as truth, the way God has recovered the truth by the men of Hezekiah, the distinct ministry we have had in the recovery. We need to pay heed to the history of the recovery, the way the enemy has been against it all the time, because the enemy will be at the life line, he will be against that which represents the living line of the testimony at any given moment. The situation of the testimony today is not the same as it was in Mr. Taylor’s time, or Mr. Raven’s time, or Mr. Darby’s time; we are living in different days and there are different needs and different circumstances, but the truth is the same, and the Lord is the same, the glorious Head of the assembly.

There has been much departure from the truth in the history of the recovery but the Lord says to Philadelphia, “Hold fast what thou hast, that no one take thy crown”, Revelation 3: 11. The Lord would credit the holding of His word. And it is a test, you know, especially when there is a trend that goes differently, to be governed by the Lord’s word. What the Lord is saying currently, and what the Spirit is saying to the assemblies, is the test.

It is a day in which the dross is being taken from the silver, as we have it here, in view of a vessel for the refiner. What a charge the Lord has given us in relation to the truth once delivered to the saints. How the enemy has been against it in the course of the recovery, and how the truth has been established, and the truth will stand. The assembly is the pillar and base of the truth. John says, “the Spirit is the truth”, (1 John 5: 6), and the Lord Jesus Himself is the truth. He is the way, and the truth, and the life (John 14: 6), and we have that reference in Ephesians 4: 21, “as the truth is in Jesus”. The assembly is here where the Lord Jesus maintained the rights of God. You remember Pilate saying to the Lord, “Thou art then a king?” The Lord says, “I have been born for this, and for this I have come into the world, that I might bear witness to the truth”, John 18: 37. The Lamb’s wife, the assembly, is in the place where the Lord Himself stood; that is where the assembly is today. There is a continuation here in the power of the Holy Spirit of what was here in Jesus. He went through death and He went into glory, and as has been said, what went up in glory came down here in the power of the Holy Spirit, and it is here in the assembly.

So that is where we are today—“As he is, we also are in this world”, 1 John 4: 17. What a vessel the assembly is! What a sense it should give to our hearts of the dignity of the place that has been given us, and as we are in the sense of the dignity of what the assembly is in the mind of God and in the, heart of Christ we shall not find it difficult to determine anything that is not in keeping with it. “Take away the dross from the silver, and there cometh forth a vessel for the refiner—take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness”, Proverbs 25: 5. That is what we would covet for each local assembly, that the Lord’s rights in local assemblies might be recognised, that the world to come may already be in evidence in the administration in each local assembly. The Lord has His direct rights in each local assembly and they are not to be interfered with, beloved brethren, and the Lord will stand by His rights. We can be assured that if the Lord addresses local assemblies in Revelation 2 and 3 there will be the element of the overcomer in the local assembly that will answer to it, even if it be but one, and such have a peculiar promise.

So it is a time of completion, the time in which the Lord Jesus is completing the dispensation, in outward weakness, in outward smallness, but in the maintenance of the truth as it is from the beginning and in the recognition of the truth as it has been ministered to us by those that have gone before. What a distinct ministry the Lord has given in this city; not that it gives any distinction to any city, because the local assembly is the local assembly—we need to see the glory and the distinction of it, and we need to have great respect for it, and for one another too. What the saints are in the mind of God is something that we need to get hold of in our hearts increasingly. I am sure we shall find that things will be working more efficiently as we appreciate the spiritual links we have together so that the functioning of the body will be promoted, and there will be in body feelings and in sensitiveness a working out or depth in a mutual way for the glory of God. The assembly is not only the vessel that has the glory of God as it comes down in administration in the world to come, but it is the vessel of glory to God throughout the eternal day. And as there is the maintenance of what is due to the Lord Jesus in each local assembly there will be in result the service of praise. The Lord Jesus died that the praise might be secured. Whatever there may be working against it by the power of the gates of hales, there is that working out in the assembly that cannot be overcome.

We were reminded locally of how in Hezekiah’s day the enemy came up against Jerusalem and the matter looked hopeless, but it brought out an element that could not be overcome; it brought out the virgin daughter of Zion who laughed at, and scorned, the enemy, and the enemy was not to shoot one arrow into the city. And the Jerusalem dwellers will be saved from the enemy; they are in a position that is unconquerable. The enemy will have no way in if you are a Jerusalem dweller. If saints are carried away it brings out that they are not Jerusalem dwellers. Jerusalem dwellers will stand, like Simeon, by the truth as it has been received. Simeon means ‘hearing’, and he was a man in Jerusalem; he was the pattern man for the rapture when he received Christ in his arms and said, “Lord, now thou lettest thy bondman go, according to thy word, in peace”, Luke 2: 29. In priestly grace his hands were filled with Christ. The end of all administration is Christ, that Christ may be seen in the gates; “Her husband is known in the gates”, as it says at the end of Proverbs, as a result of the working out of wisdom in the assembly.

So it is the glory of God to conceal a thing; it has pleased God to conceal matters from the natural mind, and we thank God for doing it. The natural mind cannot understand it but the spiritual mind will understand it; it is the glory of kings to search out a thing. Whatever our natural feelings may be, whatever the personalities that our eyes may be on, it is not a question of natural feelings, it is not a question of personalities, beloved brethren, it is what the assembly is according to God, what the house of God is as governed by divine order. And we need to hold at all cost what we have received through beloved men like Mr. Darby, Mr. Raven and Mr. Taylor. I do not know how much Mr. Taylor’s ministry has been followed up, but I am sure the brethren have the highways in their heart; it says, “Blessed is the man ... in whose heart are the highways”, Psalm 84: 5. Such will see to it that the living line is continued at the present time in the way that things are maintained in faithfulness in local assemblies. The Lord would trust the local assembly; that is where He has committed things in responsibility and we can count on Him to come in as to any matter amongst the saints. “It is the glory of God to conceal a thing”. It may be concealed, and if a thing is concealed we need to go to the Lord about it; we need to find out, beloved brethren, as Moses said, “Make me now to know thy way”, Exodus 33: 13. Think of the way Moses finished up as king in Jeshurun, the truth worked out in such a way that Moses was king in Jeshurun. May the Lord bless the word to us, for His name’s sake.

The power of God in the glad tidings is equal to any moral situation. That power is vested in the Saviour, Jesus, the Son of God. We read here of an extreme case, a man completely dominated by Satan’s power. I do not think we would find many people possessed by demons in this country, but we would find persons who are under the power of Satan, the power of darkness, unsubdued. This man was unsubdued. No one could tame him, no one could control him, neither law, nor the police, nor society, nor religion. No power seemed to be able to change this man. No power could subdue him. What a case! What a situation! A man wild under the power of Satan!—an extreme case of the gentiles under the power of Satan.

Reformation was no good for this man, latitude was no good. What did he need? He needed power from God; he needed to meet Jesus, the Saviour, the Son of God. If you meet Him, you meet a power superior to all the power of Satan and the power of the world. Did He not come into the world for that purpose—to seek and to save that which was lost? Here is a man who was lost. If you have not come to the Saviour, you are lost. If you have not believed in Jesus, you are lost, you are still in your sins. You must have contact, by faith, with Jesus for yourself, not just through your parents, and it is not sufficient just to come to the meetings.

I believe the Lord deliberately went into this country to meet this man. How gracious of the Lord, the Son of God, to meet a man who had been cast out of society, a man in this condition, full of the devil. Jesus is interested in men.
No matter what your state, what your moral history, what your sins, He is interested in you.

The love of God is towards us. “God commends his love to us, in that, we being still sinners”—(not when we were good, not when we were holy—in fact we never have been holy, but in our sins, as sinners; there is nothing to commend us, or to draw out the love of God, but the love of God is so great that it moves from its own side)—“we being still sinners—(in our filthiness and in our corruption and pride)—“Christ has died for us”, Romans 5: 8. What a wonderful love the love of God is, boundless, its motive being in itself. We usually love what is lovable, something that would draw out our love, but God’s love towards the sinner is towards what is unlovely.

So the Lord Jesus moved. There is going to be a confrontation here. The Lord Jesus meets the devil in this man, in this legion of demons. Who is going to get the victory? If you surrender to Jesus, if you cry to Jesus, we know who will get the victory. The Lord has bound the strong man. He took the sting out of death by dying and going into the domain of death Himself, and coming out triumphant. Blessed Saviour! He is a triumphant Saviour, who has power over death. He will take away from you the fear of death and the consequences of death. What a terrible thing it is to die in your sins and to meet God in your sins! There is no need to do that. The Saviour is seeking you; the Saviour is wanting you. The Saviour’s love is towards us, as it was towards this man.

So what did this man need? What do most men need? What do most christians need? Deliverance! —deliverance from the world, deliverance from the power of sin, deliverance from indwelling sin, deliverance from themselves—that is perhaps the greatest deliverance. What a deliverance that is! I would not say that I was completely delivered from self, but it is a great thing to know the power of God and the power of the Spirit, to be able to say, “The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and of death”, Romans 8: 2. That was Paul’s experience, a man who had gone through the seventh chapter of Romans. The Spirit of life in that glorious Man there, flowing into my soul, delivers me from the power and law of sin and death. That is what this man needed, did he not?—deliverance! And he got it. He came into contact with the Saviour, and he surrendered.
To get the gain of the blessing and of salvation, you must surrender. The love of God and the love of Christ would constrain you to surrender your own will. What is our own will anyway?

Contaminated and filthy! The gospel would subdue you and give you to surrender to Christ, to surrender to the Saviour. That is what this man did, and even the demons recognised that here was Jesus the Son of God. The power of God was there in that blessed Man. He was divine, of course; He was God; a blessed Man, and a Saviour too. A Man because He was to die for our sins. Is not that touching? Believers can say that in His holy body He bore our sins on the tree, took them away from the sight of God; so any sinner, of whatever nationality, whatever creed, may be saved.

Oh the value of the work of Christ, the value of the redemption, the value of the blood of Christ—the blood of such a Man! The blood of no other man could be compared with the blood of Jesus, the blood of a holy Man, the Son of God. What virtue is in the blood of Christ; what virtue in His work! He accomplished redemption that this man might have peace. What this man came into was peace, and righteousness, and control, in subjection. What a complete change! The gospel involves that, that if we are truly converted there is a complete, radical change in our ways and outlook and habits and walk. This man did not want to go back to the tombs and to the chains. Thank God for the deliverance! What a deliverance it is to be brought to Christ and delivered from this filthy world and its habits, sins, and pursuits. This man was completely delivered.

So there he is, sitting under control. What the gospel would do, according to Romans, is to bring us into righteousness, bring us into peace with God, bring us into reconciliation, bring us into joy and happiness. Have you had this transaction with the Lord? Have you really had to do with the Lord about your sins and about your will and about your pride? Have you really longed for deliverance and gone through the seventh chapter of Romans? Have you felt, ‘Oh wretched man that I am!’ and been disgusted with yourself? If you long for deliverance, you will get an answer. If you get into the tunnel, the Lord will bring you to the end of the tunnel. There is always a light at the end of a tunnel, even though it is very dark in the middle. There will be a light at the other side. It is a great thing to experience, especially in our young days as believers, something of what is spoken of in the seventh chapter of Romans. I believe that in the days of Mr. Stoney and Mr. Raven deliverance was quite a common theme, but now perhaps it is not so much spoken of. Persons do not seem to be getting into the exercises of the seventh chapter of Romans. But sooner or later, if you are a believer and you go on with God, you will be brought to these exercises. You will be brought to what you are in yourself, what the flesh is, what self is. Turn away from it in disgust, and have your life and power in another Man.

So this man was converted, really changed. He represents what the Lord is wanting for the assembly, for assembly service. He wants men like this. He wants sisters, too, who are like the woman in this chapter, healed from the issue of blood, persons who are not anaemic, but full of vitality. The woman in this chapter represents a believer whose life has been ebbing away. To apply the scripture, she still came to the meetings, but her inward life was ebbing away. Your inward life will keep ebbing away if you do not keep contact and communion with Christ, if you do not keep your living links with that Man up there. Your life will ebb away and you will become merely formal. This woman’s life was ebbing away. What was the remedy? Contact with Jesus!—breaking through the crowd! She was an overcomer. She wanted deliverance, and she got it. She touched the hem of His garment and power went out from the Lord, out from His body.

Our power comes from the Lord, too, our blessed living Head. Power can come from Him into your very soul and quicken even your body—make you feel better in health. Sometimes as you get older you feel weak and too tired to go to the meetings. What do you do? You cry to the Lord, to the Priest, and cry to the Spirit, so that power can come into you. It has been said that piety even affects your health. It is primarily for your spirit and soul, as quickened consciously with Christ, but if you get a quickening touch it can affect your body. It is a great thing to go on with the Lord daily, to go on in communion with the Lord and seek a living touch from Him. Break through like Pherez in Genesis 38: 29; be a breaker through, an overcomer.

That would be my message to you, and to myself particularly, that we might be in the gain of deliverance; that we might be delivered persons, not content with formalities or platitudes, but in life, especially in the assembly and in assembly service. This man is delivered. He is to be a testimony. He is to go home and testify to what the Lord has done, a testimony to the work and power of God. What God has done with this man He can do with me and He can do with you. He could do it with Saul of Tarsus. There is no case impossible to the Lord in the glad tidings. May the Lord bless the word!

It will be noticed that there are references to the first day of the week in the verses we have read in John’s gospel, and John on the isle of Patmos speaks about being in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, and I thought the Lord might have something to say to us as to those two terms which are used in relation to the same day.

This twentieth chapter of John tells us something about the Lord’s activities on that day on which He arose from the dead, and I believe He is a model for us as to how we would spend that day. The Lord was very active. He rose very early in the morning and He was still active in the evening. He came to the disciples in the evening when the doors were shut and He said, “Peace be to you”, so that His activities extended right throughout the day. Then in regard to the Lord’s day, it would suggest that the Lord has certain claims or rights in regard to that day, so that as we go through the Lord’s day we would not spend it in the same way as we would spend other days. We would recognise the. Lord’s claims and we would spend the day in a way which would be suitable, which would be pleasing to the Lord in regard to His day and in regard to His claims on that day.

I think we might say that in recent years there has been some progress made in regard to the assembling of ourselves for the Supper, and the time at which we do it. Probably most of us here will remember that there was a time when we did not break bread until nearly the middle of the day. Well, I believe that our brother Mr. Taylor felt that matter. He spoke about the tendency then to have a lie-in on Lord’s day morning, and he did not seem to think that that fitted in very well with the character of the day. As we know, the Lord took our brother in 1953, and it was not until Mr. McCallum’s ministry in London in 1958 that the matter came up as to having the breaking of bread earlier.

I think things have moved since then and I believe we can say that the affections of the saints for the Lord have been such that we would not desire the arrangement to be otherwise than it is. We are thankful if we can begin the day in good time, remembering the Lord as He has requested. Then as we go through the day we happily have other occasions when we come together; we come together to read the Scriptures, and also for the preaching. Then in between we go to our homes; a little visiting may be done, a little entertaining, but at any rate we spend part of the time in the homes. That is all part of the Lord’s day, and I believe that as we see what the Lord did on this day, how He was active and how He ministered to the disciples, we would seek that our activities might be in line with that, not only when we come together assembly-wise but also in our homes. We would seek to remember that it is His day.

In this scripture in the Revelation the apostle was in exile on the island called Patmos. He felt the reproach of the position; I suppose he was in isolation. We do not read of any brethren being there, but he says he became in the Spirit on the Lord’s day. It is interesting how that title is used. The apostle Paul, in writing to the Corinthians, speaks about the Lord’s supper, or the dominical supper. So the apostle John says, “I became in the Spirit on the Lord’s day”, or the dominical day. It is the day when the Lord has certain peculiar rights. It has been pointed out that when the Lord passed with His disciples through the cornfields on the sabbath He said that He was Lord of the sabbath; that is to say. He wanted His disciples to be at liberty. The Pharisees were seeking to put restrictions on the disciples as to what they were doing, but the Lord wanted them to be at liberty; He was Lord of the sabbath.

But the Lord’s day is not exactly the sabbath. It is not exactly a day for rest in that way. I remember looking a long time ago at some dictionary as to the definition of ‘Sunday’, and it said ‘the Christian sabbath’, but I do not think that is quite the right idea. I think we have been taught that the Lord’s day is a thing by itself; it is not the sabbath, but it is a day in which the Lord has rights. He is the Lord of the sabbath, but He also has rights in regard of His day, the first day of the week, and we would desire to recognise the Lord’s rights, and that our activities on that day should be in accord with His rights. We would have liberty to do certain other things on other days, but in a special way I think the Lord makes claims in regard to His day. Well, I am sure the Lord would encourage us in this way. It is wonderful, the fellowship that we have together and how we can enjoy our links with one another, and I believe that if we are in one another’s houses on the Lord’s day it is an opportunity of getting near to one another and enjoying the links that we have in what is heavenly and what is spiritual.

There is another scripture in my mind, in 1 Corinthians 13, the chapter about love. It says there that “Love never fails” (verse 8). In matters that may come up certain difficulties may arise, but if love is in operation love has a way of solving those difficulties. So Paul says, “Love never fails”. But then the apostle goes on to say (verse 11), “When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I reasoned as a child; when I became a man, I had done with what belonged to the child”. I believe that when the apostle says, “When I became a man, I had done with what belonged to the child”, he is speaking of his activities in a general way.

He is not just referring to the first day of the week, but to what he did every day. You might say that every day he had done with what belonged to the child, but I think perhaps it is a word for us. I think we would be encouraged to be on that line, of having done with what belongs to the child.

As we go through the week we may have some free time, and the thing is, what do we do? We would not want to occupy ourselves with things that belong to the child. I am sure the Lord would help us in that way and there are many things to engage us. The Lord has much teaching for us and there is much ministry that is available. We are very thankful indeed for the way that the Spirit is active, and He gives us ministry at the present time. In our comings together the Lord gives us ministry, but also we have the written ministry, much of it, and there is much labour too that enters at the present time into the preparation of current ministry so that it may be available to the saints. I believe there would be some profit in devoting some of our time to that, not simply that we have the labours of those who prepare the printed ministry, but also that we might take advantage of it and read it. I believe that that would help us to go in for what is mature. There are certain things which belong to the child which might be legitimate, and we might regard certain things as normal for children, but when we grow up we would want to be matured and we would not want to occupy our time needlessly with things which could be done without and which are really in themselves childish.

Well, my desire is that we might be helped in this way and encouraged, and the Lord is a wonderful example to us. The first day of the week is a day of special privilege, and it is a day when we are free. We have activities which rightly engage us during the week, when we are not so free, but on the Lord’s day we are free and it is a privilege to be able to use our freedom in a way which will be profitable, which will be for our building up and edification, and which will render praise to God too, as He sees something being worked out amongst us, something that builds us up in our souls. I am sure we all desire to be built up and to grow.

We are, I trust, growing and we would desire that our growth should continue, because there is a time coming when growth will cease. How good it is if we are occupied with what belongs to manhood; that would mean that we continue in growth, and so we find we make progress, we find some lasting satisfaction, something which will be for good and for profit.

So one trusts that we might be encouraged to think of the Lord’s activities as a model for us, that we should be active in that way, and too that we should recognise His claims and order our pathway in a way which is pleasing to Him, both in regard to how we spend the Lord’s day and also in our activities in a general way. If there is any time we have at our disposal, in which we may have a choice of activities, we would seek to use it in a way which would be comely for the position that we are in. Children and young people might have certain activities, but as we grow older we would seek to do what is normal to those who are matured, and so the Lord would help us. I trust that we may be encouraged in this way. As we think of the greatness of divine things, what we have in the Scriptures, and that we have the Spirit to open them up to us, how wonderful it is—well worth while going in for! So may we be encouraged on this line, and may the Lord help us, for His name’s sake.
Jesus our Lord, ‘tis the joy of Thy presence
Calls forth response to Thy love from our hearts;
Thy name as ointment poured forth in its fragrance
Now to Thy lovers its sweetness imparts.
For Thou hast come to us, Lord, in Thy glory,
Thou mighty Victor all praises above,
Bowing our souls in true homage before Thee,
Filling our hearts with the warmth of Thy love.
Lord, in Thy manhood, as risen, victorious,
Thou our affections so wholly hast won,
Yet in Thy Person divine and so glorious
Thee we would worship as God’s blessed Son.
Fruit of Thy death for Thy heart’s satisfaction,
Of Thee and like Thee. Thy heavenly bride
Gladly responds to Thine own love’s attraction,
Suited companion to be at Thy side.
So now, blest Lord, we are joyfully giving
To Thee love’s answer, Thine own treasured part;
Worthy art Thou as exalted and living
Of all that meets the desires of Thy heart.
Aberdeen

“A HELPMATE, HIS LIKE” This expression in Genesis 2: 18 sets out the divine thought of what a wife is to be. Ephesians 5 shows that Genesis 2 relates to both the truth of Christ and the assembly and to the marriage bond. What an advantage it is to a man to have a helpmate, and in how many ways a wife can be indispensable to her husband. But there is this additional thought—“his like”. That is, she is to be just like her husband, one with him in his outlook, exercises, and desires. Thus she can support and help him in them. Aquila and Priscilla are a fine example of a husband and wife who were one in the things of the Lord.

The husband, in his place of headship, will, if things are right, have the Lord’s interests as his first priority—but he is certainly not to be unpractical as to home responsibilities. The wife is to encourage her husband in his desires to be devoted to the Lord and His interests, so she will not be too possessive as to him, thus making it easier for him to make time for the Lord’s things. It will mean sacrifice, but she will be blessed for that.

“His like” would also mean that what a brother seeks to support in word and conduct is backed up by his wife’s character. His expounding on headship will be undermined if she is insubject; his exhortation on heavenly-mindedness could certainly have the edge taken off it if she is earthly-minded.

It is testing and searching to reflect on the divine standard, but let us seek grace to answer to it, for heaven loves to see man and wife set together in support of the testimony of our Lord, and there is real joy and blessing in it.

The Lord is aiming at the greatest possible product; but the church is to be the acme of divine workmanship and He is pleased to use us in that. So it is a question of one’s ability for refining, that is, the increase in quality in the ministry. The heavenly city will be the fulness of the result of that work, the excess. The superlative degree is in Ephesians, and that points to the work of God in its completeness. The heavenly city really will display the supreme refining work of God, and that is what should affect us if the Lord is pleased to call us into His service; are we able to move on into a little bit of quality in ministry? It is not simply volume; quality is the thing to which the Lord would call attention.

To be in real service ... you must insist on yourself being the model of what you preach. Be able always to say, like Gideon, ‘Do as I do’. Paul was always the model of what he taught, and I do not believe any of us effect for others in our ministry more than what the Spirit has effected in ourselves. If the ministry be of divine power, and adapted to a believer for his acceptance, surely it must begin with the minister.
